definition: Pattern recognition is a very active field of research intimately bound to machine learning.
details: Also known as classification or statistical classification, pattern recognition aims at building a classifier that can determine the class of an input pattern. This procedure, known as training, corresponds to learning an unknown decision function based only on a set of input-output pairs ( x i , y i ) {\displaystyle ({\boldsymbol {x}}_{i},y_{i})} that form the training data (or training set). Nonetheless, in real world applications such as character recognition, a certain amount of information on the problem is usually known beforehand. The incorporation of this prior knowledge into the training is the key element that will allow an increase of performance in many applications.

explainer.lead: Prior knowledge for pattern recognition concerns using information beyond the training input-output pairs to help build a classifier. It matters because real applications such as character recognition rarely supply enough data alone.

tiers.eli5: When examples are few, you give the learner some background hints so it doesn't have to figure everything out from scratch.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers inject domain knowledge to supplement training data that only provides input-output pairs. A pitfall is relying on wrong or overly rigid priors, which can bias the learned decision function.
tiers.paperLevel: Pattern recognition, also called classification or statistical classification, aims to build a classifier that determines the class of an input pattern; training learns an unknown decision function from input-output pairs, but real applications such as character recognition require a certain amount of additional information.

explainer.example: In character recognition, telling the classifier that certain stroke shapes are unlikely helps it generalize from limited labeled examples.
